title: A measure finite on compact sets admits no infinite disjoint family of uniformly heavy sets inside a ball
statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let μ be a Borel measure on ℝ^P with μ(K) ≠ ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P. Let r ∈ ℝ and c ∈ [0, ∞] with c ≠ 0, and let (D_i)_{i∈ℕ} be Borel subsets of ℝ^P such that D_i ∩ D_j = ∅ whenever i ≠ j, D_i ⊆ B_r(0) and c ≤ μ(D_i) for every i. Then these assumptions are contradictory, i.e. the conclusion is False.
lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (D : ℕ → Set (Euclid P)) (r : ℝ) (c : ℝ≥0∞), (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → μ K ≠ ∞) → c ≠ 0 → (∀ i, MeasurableSet (D i)) → (∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (D i) (D j)) → (∀ i, D i ⊆ ball 0 r) → (∀ i, c ≤ μ (D i)) → False
